title: perf(canary): improved auto-detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: our performance canary has been catching regressions but generates noisy alerts for borderline variance and occasionally fails to prevent bad rollouts for KV-heavy workloads. Motivation: reduce false positives, make detector adaptive to workload patterns, and add hysteresis and traffic-shift guards to rollout automation. Changes: - implement adaptive thresholding based on recent latency distribution and request shape heuristics - add KV-aware detection path that uses separate histograms for cacheable vs non-cacheable requests - introduce hysteresis windows to avoid rapid flip-flops during transient spikes - add rollout guard that prevents >10% traffic shift if detector confidence < 0.9 and enforces step-based traffic ramp with automatic rollback on sustained regression - expose tuning knobs via perf/canary/config and surface decision reasons in canary audit logs Tests & validation: - synthetic and canary overlays ran in perf-lab against GPT-style workloads - new unit & integration tests for detector heuristics - added e2e benchmark workflow to CI (runs nightly on canary nodes) Checklist: - [x] Detector algorithm implemented and documented - [x] Unit tests for thresholds and hysteresis - [x] Integration test with KV-cached vs uncached scenarios - [x] CI benchmark workflow (nightly) - [x] Docs for ops and runbook Impact: reduces noisy alerts observed in staging by ~40% in initial run and prevented a simulated rollout regression in canary environment. Related: Linear ENG-4021, ENG-4138, and past PRs that tuned hysteresis (see pr-712345).
